PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single responsibility in a test helps pinpoint failures. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if only one method call/behavior is tested; non-compliant if multiple Acts are present. DECISION RULES: (1) Count distinct Act operations; if >1 mark non-compliant. Here the test constructs an instance (constructor) and separately calls a static method MaxMin1.maxMin1(...) — two distinct Act operations. (2) Test name 'test3' is generic but not the primary signal here. (3) There are clearly two assertion groups corresponding to the two Acts. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on other tests. RATIONALE: Independence allows arbitrary ordering/parallel execution. DECISION RULES: No @Before/@After needed because method uses only local variables; no static/instance mutated. VERDICT: compliant.
